new_marks:
Top band (5 marks): A developed explanation covering: Vatican II (1962–65) produced Gaudium et Spes, which affirmed that death is the moment when the 'riddle of human existence' becomes most acute, and that the resurrection answers it; the council reformed the funeral rite to emphasise resurrection hope; Lumen Gentium re-centred the Church as 'the people of God' sharing in the paschal mystery; post-council encyclicals (Evangelium Vitae 65 on euthanasia, Salvifici Doloris on suffering) continued this development.

Lower-mid band (2 marks): One influence described without reference to specific documents.
Low band (1 mark): Brief mention of Vatican II without substance.
